datasets.title: Thailand - Satellite detected water extents in Doi Tao District, Chiang Mai Province as of 6 October 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20240912THA This map illustrates satellite-detected water in Doi Tao District, Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, acquired on 6 October 2024 at 13:16 LT. Within the analysed area of approximately 800 km², about 54 km² of land appears to be affected by floodwaters, with around 30 km² of cropland inundated. Based on WorldPop spatial demographic data, approximately 140 people are exposed to or living near the flooded areas. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/water-extents-in-doi-tao-district-chiang-mai-province-as-of-6-october-2024]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts processed optical satellite imagery acquired on 6 October 2024, comparing multi-temporal images to detect notable changes in water extent. Water-classified pixels were extracted and vectorized to delineate inundated areas. Exposure was estimated by overlaying the flood extent with WorldPop gridded population data and land use classification to quantify affected population and cropland.
